messages:
Ryan: Canaries in eu-west-2 started failing shortly after today's driver push. H100 hosts are exhibiting kernel load errors on several workloads — 3/4 canaries failed. Anyone else seeing this?
InfraBot: deploy-bot: driver-rollout v2.3.0 -> eu-west-2 started at 1712367000 :rotating_light:
Maria: Can you paste the exact error logs from the agent(s)? sm90 vs PTX mismatch would be my first guess.
Ryan: Pasting the node agent output from one of the failed canaries:```
E kernel_loader: failed to load cubin for module 'lm_head'
  cudaErrorUnknown: PTX version 'sm_90' not supported by driver
  kernel_link: unresolved symbol __nv_cubin_func
  stack: /var/log/runner/loader.log:62
```
Samir: That looks like the driver can't JIT PTX->cubin for SM90. Do we know which driver binary the rollout installed?
Taylor: The rollout package used nvidia-driver-535.54-rc1 that we staged yesterday. Looking at release notes there was a min-driver change for SM90 in newer CUDA toolkits. Some runtimes expect driver >= 535.90 but we didn't gate the rollout. Also seeing NCCL init errors on the same hosts: `ncclCommInitRank failed: unhandled cuda error`.
Maria: Two immediate mitigation options: 1) revert drivers on canaries (fast) or 2) instruct serving runtime to prefer precompiled cubins (sm86) as a downgrade for affected models. Which is lower risk?
Ryan: I reverted the canary driver to the previous stable image and the canaries recovered (running health checks now). However, a couple of production jobs pinned to the new model variant still failed to start. Revert fixed scheduling but not model compatibility.
Samir: Short term: pause rollout globally and mark eu-west-2 driver rollout as failed. Label affected host pools so autoscaler doesn't reimage them. Medium term: add a driver-min-version check in the rollout pipeline and have the serving runtime detect PTX/cubin mismatch and automatically select a compatible model artifact.
Taylor: I'll add a preflight `cuobjdump --ptx <module>` check in the CI that compares the module's PTX arch to driver-reported supported archs. Also adding a Prometheus alert: `kernel_load_errors / total_kernel_loads > 0.001` over 5m.
InfraBot: incident-bot: created INC-2026-0423-driver-sm90-compat (priority P2) - https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-0423
Maria: Cost/ops note: rolling back and re-provisioning pools costs extra scheduling churn; estimate ~12 GPU-hours per affected pool + additional support pager time. We should include that in the postmortem.
Ryan: Agreed. Putting Samir and Taylor on action items. @Samir please own postmortem and include: rollout gates, runtime fallback, per-region driver matrix, and canary preflight tests.
Samir: On it. I'll start a draft after we confirm all hosts are stable. Also recommend we version-lock exported cubins for critical production models to avoid PTX JIT in the hot path.
Maria: One more thing — check our Dedicated customers who pinned driver updates in their VPCs. We may need to notify them proactively if their runtime auto-applied the same driver.
Ryan: Good call. I'll loop in customer success with a brief and a remediation plan. Thanks all :thumbsup:
